01 · The Problem

Two groups.
One unmet need.

01
The Workers
Entrepreneurs, freelancers, and remote workers couldn't afford traditional office or co-working space. Home was full of distractions. Coffee shops felt unwelcoming. There was nowhere designed for productive, flexible work.
02
The Venues
Hotels, cafes, and restaurants had significant underutilised daytime capacity. They wanted more foot traffic but had no structured way to attract and retain a working crowd reliably.

"The problem wasn't a lack of spaces. It was a lack of structure, trust, and value exchange. Nobody had solved the match."

The app in the real world

03 · The Solution

Work out the box.
The WealthSpaces model.

WealthSpaces connected remote workers with hotels, cafes, and restaurants offering co-working-ready spaces. Members paid a monthly subscription. Venues got increased daytime trade and a revenue share.

Three subscription tiers
Essential
R99/month — Township entrepreneurs
Entry-level access to WealthSpaces network. Inclusive pricing for South Africa's emerging market.
Classic
R249/month — Freelancers and SMEs
Free coffee, Wi-Fi, parking, 20% food discount, meeting rooms, Raha Rewards, networking events.
Premium
R449/month — Corporate and teams
Full benefits plus team management, priority bookings, and extended perks.

06 · Honest Reflection

What went
wrong.

WealthSpaces taught me more about product management than any course ever could. I share these failures openly — because they shaped how I think about every product decision today.

Vanity Metrics
We celebrated downloads, not retention
Top 10 downloaded app felt like success. But downloads are an acquisition metric. Users were leaving and we weren't measuring why.
Premature Build
New features before validating the MVP
We got excited by early traction and added features instead of sitting with the MVP long enough to understand what users actually needed.
Wrong Response
Treated a product problem as a marketing problem
When retention dropped, we increased marketing. We were solving the wrong problem. The issue was core experience, not awareness.
Supply Imbalance
Venues signed up but weren't properly activated
Low user frequency meant venues deprioritised WealthSpaces. Out of sight, out of mind. Both sides of the marketplace needed equal attention.
Problem Fit
We assumed the problem at the scale we needed it
We validated demand in surveys, but not behaviour change. Would people actually change where they work? That question needed deeper discovery.
07 · The Through-Line

The product is never
the point.

The person is the point. Every lesson from WealthSpaces now lives in how I approach user research, problem framing, and product decisions.
